keyFindings.description: GitHub reports the head `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` against main: 10 ahead, 71 behind. A conflicting pull request starts no `on: pull_request` workflow at all, so nothing further can be judged at a head in that state and an approval there would pin something that must move anyway. This is independent of the finding below and would hold the round on its own. The forward merge is the first item of the next round; the compare of the current code head with the branch head still prints only `.legion/` paths, so the lane read below stands for the code that is there now.

Text this change wrote says every launch provisions the workspace afresh, which is false for the ordinary case and in four places. `docs/kubernetes.md:750-752`: 'every launch of a claim — a resume in a pod of its own making, and a resume in a pod created after the last one went — provisions its workspace from the issue's pushed branch … anything it had not pushed went with the pod before it'. The enumeration names two cases, both of which create a pod, and the opener generalises over all launches; the omitted third case is the common one. `internal/runtime/sandbox/podkind.go:85-87` states it flatly with no enumeration at all: 'every launch, a resume included, provisions its workspace afresh'. `docs/kubernetes.md:1214-1215` ('as every launch does now') and `:3876-3877` ('so every launch provisions the workspace afresh') repeat it. The mechanism: `relaunch.go:123-128` keeps a live, undrifted pod whose addresses have not moved, and `l.kind.provision` is called only inside the `if replace` branch (`:166`); a launch into a kept pod goes to `recordAddresses` and `launchers.start` (`:213-218`), and `relaunch_test.go:147-160` pins that a role start does not reinitialise the issue. Five of an issue's six roles start into the pod the first launch created, so the sentence is wrong about the majority of launches and tells a reader that a role start loses unpushed work, which it does not. What is true is that every *new or replacement pod* provisions afresh. Both thermonuclear passes reached this independently; I verified it against `relaunch.go` before filing.
keyFindings.structuralNote: The quality pass's observation is worth carrying into the fix rather than fixing four sentences four times: this is one contract — pod lifetime versus role lifetime — expanded in four places, and the sites disagree only because each expansion was written separately. Stating it once and referring to it is the repair that stops the fifth.

thermonuclear.codeQuality: CHANGES — the same finding, reached independently, with the structural note above. Its sweep names what it searched for; it reports no dead state, no orphaned golden and no new size threshold crossed, and it answered the question I asked about why these lifecycle sentences keep being wrong: the two round-11 errors sat on different boundaries — workflow decides when to stop, the runtime decides what stopping deletes — so no single contract would have caught both; the every-launch claim is the one case of genuine prose duplication.
thermonuclear.independence: As stated in the pull request body: separate agents, separate prompts, separate reads of the source, neither told about the other. Not a claim about model family; nobody has read .message.provider or .message.model for those sessions.
